conventions.convention: Coordinate vectors are columns; the standard complex inner product is linear in its first argument, adjoints are conjugate transposes, and matrix norms are induced operator norms.
The matrix exponential is the operator-norm convergent series e^(zA)=Σ(k≥0) z^k A^k/k!, with A^0=I_d and d≥1.
The propagator solves iℏ ∂tU=H(t)U; ω=2π/T; monodromy eigenphases are exp(−iTε/ℏ), and quasienergies are classes ε+ℏωℤ without a preferred real branch. Countable Choice is assumed.

The Sambe space uses unnormalized measure dt on (0,T); K=H−iℏD has componentwise periodic H¹ domain, with endpoint traces taken from absolutely continuous representatives. Fourier modes are T^(−1/2)exp(inωt), n∈ℤ. AC and Countable Choice are assumed.
Fourier indices run from −N through N in increasing order; H(t)=Σ H_k exp(ikωt), H_(−k)=H_k*, and coefficients outside bandwidth b are zero. Row n, column m receives H_(n−m)+nℏωδ_nm I_d.
The eigensolver is a caller-supplied total routine with a stipulated orthonormal-basis and residual interface. Assembly returns its record unchanged and does not independently certify residuals.
The truncation estimate concerns finite Hermitian matrices and orthogonal projections, includes every real time and the projections 0 and I, and asserts no convergence for unbounded coupling.

load_bearing.statement: For A∈M_d(ℂ), d≥1, and z∈ℂ, e^(zA):=Σ(k≥0) z^k A^k/k!, A^0=I_d; this series converges absolutely in operator norm.
For d≥1, A=A* on standard ℂ^d and ℏ>0, E_A(t)=exp(−itA/ℏ) is unitary for real t, E_A(t+s)=E_A(t)E_A(s), and E_A′(t)=−iAE_A(t)/ℏ=−iE_A(t)A/ℏ in operator norm.

Assuming Countable Choice, for d≥1, T>0, ℏ>0 and continuous T-periodic Hermitian H:ℝ→M_d(ℂ), the unitary propagator admits U(t,0)=P(t)exp(−itH_F/ℏ), with H_F Hermitian and P periodic unitary. Its monodromy eigenvalues are exp(−iTε_j/ℏ), and each real lift ε_j is determined modulo ℏωℤ, where ω=2π/T.

Assuming AC and Countable Choice, for d≥1, T>0, ℏ>0 and C¹ T-periodic Hermitian H, K=H−iℏD is self-adjoint on exactly the componentwise periodic H¹ domain in L²((0,T),dt;ℂ^d). The functions T^(−1/2)exp(inωt)P(t)v_j, 1≤j≤d and n∈ℤ, form an orthonormal basis with eigenvalues ε_j+nℏω.

Under AC and Countable Choice, take integers d≥1 and b,N≥0, positive ℏ,ω,τ, finite Fourier coefficients satisfying H_(−k)=H_k*, and a total solver S_τ with the declared interface. Assign every block (K_N)_nm=H_(n−m)+nℏωδ_nm I_d for −N≤n,m≤N, call S_τ(K_N) once, and return the matrix and solver record.

Under its stated AC, Countable Choice, Fourier-polynomial and total-solver hypotheses, K_N is the Hermitian matrix of Π_NK restricted to the finite Fourier subspace. Assembly uses exactly (2N+1)² block assignments and the complete procedure terminates after one solver call. No finite-section convergence, spectral-accuracy or additional residual guarantee is asserted.

seams_checked.note: Both page inventories and the spectral-method statements were checked. This is a page-order prerequisite; the assigned Floquet items do not invoke a form-spectral item or transfer semibounded min–max conclusions to the two-sided Sambe spectrum.

The page requires Floquet control, but its four items do not cite a batch-55 result as a logical premise. Their conforming Ritz, full-operator residual and propagation claims do not turn the Floquet compression theorem into a finite-section convergence or certification theorem.

The actual uses are F4 and the trace calculations in thm-qsmx-exchange-lie-weight-blocks and thm-qsmx-klr-character-specialization. Both faithfully use def-nrqmx-finite-hermitian-matrix-exponential for operator-norm convergence of the series for every finite complex matrix. The supplier Definition is general despite its Hermitian-qualified ID.
